query: when to use redux vs context react interview question

competitors.label: How do you decide between using React state, context, and external state managers?
competitors.selectionReason: GreatFrontEnd answers the same interview decision between local state, Context and external stores, including Redux Toolkit and server-state tools.
theirStrengths: A broad, current decision guide with a quick table and a separate server-state section.
Short working snippets for useState, useReducer, Context, Redux Toolkit, Zustand and TanStack Query, plus React 19 Context syntax.
theirGaps: Nothing on useSelector reference equality, unstable selector results or memoized selectors.
Form state is a single table row and URL state is not covered.

followUpConfusion: A selector that builds a new array or object therefore re-renders its component after every action anywhere in the app
React-Redux has subscribed through React's useSyncExternalStore hook since version 8

realWorldUseCases: They tie each tool to realistic situations (theme, locale, feature flags, many unrelated consumers, server caches); our dashboard and product-grid cases are more concrete but not enough to call a win.
actionableExamples: They show working code for six approaches, including Zustand and TanStack Query; we show fewer tools but add a before-and-after selector fix, so examples stay tied.
followUpConfusion: They explain Context re-renders and server state well, but skip the === comparison in useSelector, the dev-mode stability warning and concurrent-safe subscriptions.

realWorldUseCases: Add one production case where Redux was the wrong home, such as a modal open flag dispatched through the store, and show which components re-rendered.
actionableExamples: Add a short Zustand store with a selector next to the Redux Toolkit slice, so the Zustand-or-Redux follow-up has code.

competitors.label: Redux FAQ: When should I use Redux?
competitors.selectionReason: The Redux maintainers' own answer to when Redux is worth it is the canonical source for this interview question.
theirStrengths: Authoritative caution that not every app needs Redux, with the conditions where it helps most.
theirGaps: No concrete app scenario, no code and no guidance on where non-Redux state should live.

realWorldUseCases: The provider builds a new value object on every keystroke, so every consumer re-renders
actionableExamples: Lift it to the closest common parent and pass props
createSelector returns the same array until state.products.items changes

realWorldUseCases: The FAQ lists general conditions (state needed in many places, frequent updates, complex logic, larger teams, tracing changes) without a concrete app scenario.
actionableExamples: The FAQ answer has no code and no worked example.
followUpConfusion: It answers the main confusion directly: not all apps need Redux, with quotes from Pete Hunt and Dan Abramov; we add selector and Context follow-ups, but the core caution is the same.
Add the follow-up on combining Redux with a query cache, using RTK Query as the answer, since the FAQ only says other tools exist.

competitors.winReason: The FAQ is the authoritative caution against Redux by default, but it stays at general conditions; our page turns them into a kind-of-state table, a production re-render case and runnable patterns.

competitors.label: Why React Context is Not a "State Management" Tool (and Why It Doesn't Replace Redux)
competitors.selectionReason: The Redux maintainer's long-form explanation is the strongest tutorial on the Context-versus-Redux confusion this question tests.
theirStrengths: The most thorough treatment of Context as a transport mechanism and of what Redux adds.
A detailed use-case summary for Context, useReducer, both together, and Redux.
theirGaps: Its only code blocks show a Context provider and consumer.
Written in 2021: no selector identity, no Redux Toolkit code and RTK Query described as upcoming.

actionableExamples: The query cache owns fetching, caching, deduplication and refetching

realWorldUseCases: It lists many real Redux and Context use cases (traceability, middleware, replayable bug reports, sharing logic across UI layers), as broad as ours.
actionableExamples: Its code shows only a Context provider and consumer; there is no Redux, selector or server-cache code.
followUpConfusion: It covers the Context-versus-Redux misconceptions, including Context plus useReducer as a Redux replacement, in more depth; we cover different follow-ups, so this stays tied.

realWorldUseCases: Add a concrete warning sign that Context has outgrown its job, such as several state contexts that re-render the same consumers.
followUpConfusion: Expand the Context plus useReducer point into its own follow-up that lists what it lacks: selective subscriptions, middleware and DevTools.
